subject: ACME privacy intake — DPA scope & execution preference
messages:
From: Alice Evans <alice.evans@acme.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Reed <tim.reed@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: DPA and transfer scope for Acme pilot

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. We need to get the privacy paperwork in motion so we can start the pilot next month. Attached is our short privacy intake / questionnaire that legal has asked us to complete. Our two immediate asks: 1) a copy of Redwood's standard DPA or a statement of your data processing terms; and 2) confirmation of what subprocessors you use and whether you rely on any EU/UK transfer mechanisms (SCCs, UK Addendum, or adequacy).

Can you point me to the right person to handle the DPA exchange and let me know whether you prefer DocuSign or AdobeSign for signature?

Thanks,
Alice
—
Alice Evans
Procurement Lead, Acme Corp
alice.evans@acme.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Evans <alice.evans@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA and transfer scope for Acme pilot

Hi Alice — appreciate the prompt. I'm looping in Laura from Legal and Marcus from Privacy/Ops so you have direct points of contact.

Laura — can you share our current DPA template (PDF) and confirm the canonical list of subprocessors? We typically provide the DPA and a dataflow summary; for EU/UK customers we also include SCCs or the UK transfer addendum when requested. Acme's intake indicates some EU data in scope — Alice, could you flag which products/regions will send data to Redwood?

On signatures: we support DocuSign by default, but can do AdobeSign if your procurement requires it.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alice Evans <alice.evans@acme.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:43:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood DPA & a couple of clarifying points

Hi Alice — nice to meet you over email. Attaching our standard DPA (redwood_dpa_template_v1.pdf) and a one-page dataflow that Marcus prepared. A few clarifying points before we exchange redlines:

- Subprocessors: we provide a current list in Annex A of the DPA and publish updates on our subprocessor page; we can include an exportable CSV if that helps procurement.
- Transfers: Redwood operates in multiple regions. For transfers from the EU/UK to the US, our standard approach is to execute the EU SCCs (2021 module) and add the UK addendum where applicable. If Acme requires reliance on an approved adequacy decision only, please flag that.
- Incident reporting / breach notification timelines are in Section 6 of the DPA; we can discuss any specific SLAs you need for the pilot.

If you'd like to redline the PDF, send back a Word copy or track changes doc and we will review. Our legal team prefers DocuSign for execution but will accept AdobeSign if Acme has a strict vendor binding.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Tim Reed <tim.reed@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Acme redlines and questions (attached)

Laura / Grace — attaching our redlines (acme_redlines_20260115.docx). High level: we asked for (1) explicit subprocessor names and onboarding dates rather than a link-only approach; (2) a carveout to permit limited analytics processing by a managed-service partner in Ireland; and (3) clarification that Redwood will provide SCCs/UK addendum when transfers are necessary — we want the documents attached to the execution package, not handled as a separate post-signature process.

Also, one procurement note: Acme's security team asks for a brief dataflow diagram that shows where production logs are stored and whether logs include PII. Marcus — can you confirm whether logs might contain PII and the retention windows?

Thanks — Tim
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tim Reed <tim.reed@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme redlines and questions (attached)

Hi Tim — quick answers below and attaching a one-page dataflow (dataflow_summary_acme.png).

- Subprocessors: current roster is in Annex A; we can export a dated CSV with onboarding timestamps. I will add a sentence to the DPA that we will provide a current copy of Annex A with the executed DPA and post notifications for any changes.
- Analytics partner in Ireland: that is an approved subprocessor for aggregated telemetry; we do not share raw PII with that partner. Production logs may contain identifiers (user IDs and timestamps) that, in isolation, are not direct identifiers. If you consider those identifiers PII, we can add contractual limits and a retention cap. Standard log retention is 90 days for production logs and 365 days for longer-term audit retained in a separate, access-restricted store.
- SCCs/UK addendum: Laura will attach the standard EU SCCs as part of the signature package. We agree that having the SCCs bundled with the executed DPA is the cleanest approach.

On signature tooling: DocuSign is preferred operationally because our legal ops pipeline auto-archives DocuSign envelopes and attaches Annex A and SCCs at execution. If Acme must use AdobeSign, we can still accommodate but manual steps will be required.

Let me know if you want a short call for the security team to review the dataflow.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Alice Evans <alice.evans@acme.com>

Thanks everyone — the answers are helpful. Two operational items before we close the intake: 1) please bundle the current Annex A (subprocessors CSV) and the EU SCCs + UK addendum with the DocuSign envelope so our legal can review the executed set; and 2) we prefer DocuSign for the envelope.

If you can send the DocuSign envelope with the redlined DPA and supporting exhibits by Friday, Jan 23, that gives us time to route for signature and start the pilot on Feb 1.

I'll mark the HubSpot deal as "privacy intake submitted" once we receive the envelope.

Best,
Alice
